document_kind: proposed acceptance-example register; not a runtime API/schema contract
status: local draft; owner requirements/UX approval pending; independently unreviewed
scope: Twelve worked examples for requirements/acceptance walkthroughs only. No application code, parser, database, AWS loading or external publication was run.
global_labels: SYNTHETIC: source-backed fixture amounts and newly proposed toy amounts are artificial, not observed market data or owner holdings.
Only instrument_id values reuse real identities from the existing synthetic catalogue; synthetic document/account/transaction/receipt/revision labels are artificial identifiers.
Source references are repository-relative paths resolved from the repository root; JSON pointers identify inspected value locations.
Decimal monetary values are encoded as strings. Null represents unknown/unavailable data; unknown values must never silently become zero.

Kinds distinguish existing synthetic source fixtures from new proposed worked examples and new proposed fault injections. A fault injection is a requirement scenario, not evidence that the application passed it.
No example approves an otherwise unresolved policy, provider right, paid call, retention period, recovery target, architecture, numerical default or implementation.

schema_notes.story_id_range: L1-S01–L1-S16; local planning IDs, not Jira issue keys
schema_notes.instrument_identity_evidence: Catalogue entries read locally; no claim of newly verified live listing/provider availability.

validation.method: Python Decimal arithmetic and source JSON assertions; JSON/ID/story/path checks. No application tests or independent review.

XIRR_ambiguity.expected_result: ambiguous; xirr null; neither first root nor zero substituted

examples.title: SYNTHETIC large staged import survives a crash without partial financial visibility
examples.status: proposed acceptance example; no application implementation claim

given.staging: bounded batches sized from validated item/byte/service constraints
given.fault: crash after some staging batches and before the completed commit marker

when: Stage the large synthetic import under one logical identity.
Crash mid-stage, read all financial views, then retry/resume the same logical commit and finish its validated completion transition.

during_partial_staging.financial_visibility: none of the uncompleted import rows

after_valid_completion.financial_visibility: the validated completed import through its completed marker/read boundary

expected.cleanup_financial_effect: abandoned staging never changes financial state

assumptions: Ten thousand is an artificial input row count, not a promised supported limit or generated/executed fixture.
Exact ledger-row fanout, item sizes and service transaction count are deliberately unspecified; source rows need not map one-to-one to writes.
This is a proposed staging/visibility acceptance contract, not implemented DynamoDB behavior.
pending_decision_notes: Final maximum import size, batch sizing, staging expiry/recovery, completion concurrency/read-model contract and reconciliation evidence require design and validation.
No RPO, RTO, retention or cloud operation is approved by this example.

examples.title: SYNTHETIC XIRR golden, ambiguous-root and incomplete-document cases
examples.status: proposed acceptance example; no application implementation claim

ambiguous_roots_variant.day_count_basis: ACT/365 with exact elapsed days 0/365/730 for this toy assertion
ambiguous_roots_variant.note: New artificial ambiguity variant, not sourced from the existing golden fixture.

when: Evaluate the complete two-cash-flow mathematical golden case.
Separately assess whether the six-event statement excerpt can establish portfolio XIRR.
Separately evaluate the artificial three-flow case at both candidate roots; inspect ambiguity instead of selecting whichever root a solver finds first.

incomplete_statement_case.status: unavailable - incomplete dated external cash-flow history

ambiguous_roots_variant.status: ambiguous - more than one admissible root; no single authoritative XIRR

source_refs.use: Existing complete synthetic mathematical known-answer case; amounts/dates read and Decimal result verified.
Statement explicitly has incomplete history and six recent events.

assumptions: The golden pair is a mathematical check, not a forecast, realised owner return or proof of general solver correctness.
One cash outflow followed by a positive terminal amount exactly 365 days later gives one positive root in this case.
The ambiguity variant has exactly the stated annual intervals. Its zero NPV residual is evaluated through a common-denominator polynomial with Decimal to avoid repeating-decimal cancellation noise.
pending_decision_notes: Production XIRR cash-flow boundary, day count, solver tolerance, multiple/no-root behavior and eligibility still require specification; this example does not approve all conventions.
